takeaway: The breast is supplied by the internal thoracic artery (a subclavian branch), the lateral thoracic and thoracoacromial arteries (axillary branches), and in part by the intercostal arteries.

question.text: Before a mastectomy for breast cancer, which one of the following statements regarding the anatomy of the breast is correct?

answer.text: The breast is supplied in part by the intercostal arteries.

lines.text: The internal thoracic artery is a branch of the subclavian artery, and it supplies the breast.
The lateral thoracic and thoracoacromial arteries are branches of the axillary artery.
So the supply is not only from the thoracic arteries, and not completely from the subclavian branches.
Further blood supply comes from the intercostal arteries.
It is important to include this area when performing a mastectomy and examining the breast.
So the breast is supplied in part by the intercostal arteries.
